memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'You will pursue your enemies, and they will fall by the sword before
you. Five of you will chase a hundred, and a hundred of you will chase
ten thousand, and your enemies will fall by the sword before you'"
- Lev 26:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The picture here is of astonishing victory — five chasing a hundred, a
hundred routing ten thousand. The numbers do not add up by ordinary
military logic. They only make sense if God Himself was fighting for
His people.

That was exactly the point. Israel's strength was never in their numbers
or weapons. Their victories, when they came, came because the Lord went
before them.

We should not read this as a promise that Christians will win every
earthly battle, or that faith guarantees triumph over every opponent.
This was covenant language for national Israel. But the truth beneath it
endures: the battles that matter most are won by God, not by our own
strength.

Dear friend, you face battles that are far too big for you — against
temptation, fear, despair, the pull of old habits. If you fight these in
your own strength, you will lose. But you do not fight alone.

Paul reminds us that our struggle is not against flesh and blood, and
that our weapons are not the world's weapons but have divine power (2 Cor
10:4; Eph 6:12). He declares that in all these things we are more than
conquerors through Him who loved us (Rom 8:37).

The victory is not in your ability to overpower your enemies. It is in
the God who fights for you. Stand in His strength today, not your own.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What battle am I trying to fight in my own strength?
2. Do I truly believe God fights for me?
3. How would today look if I trusted God with the struggle I face?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, the battles I face are bigger than I am. Thank You that You fight
for Your people. Help me stand in Your strength rather than my own today.
Amen.
